test_title: PYST 21: RRB NTPC (UG) CBT-I - GA (Held On: 18 Aug, 2025 Shift 3)
subject: general
question: The opening of which of the following canals intensified British control over India’s foreign trade?
solution:
The correct answer is __**Suez Canal**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **Suez Canal**, connecting the **Mediterranean Sea** and the **Red Sea**, was opened in **1869**. It significantly shortened the maritime route between Europe and India, eliminating the need to circumnavigate the southern tip of Africa.
 
• The canal's opening allowed the **British Empire** to strengthen its control over trade routes to India, which was considered the "Jewel in the Crown" of the British Empire due to its economic and strategic importance.
 
• The Suez Canal facilitated quicker transportation of **goods, military supplies, and personnel**, which bolstered British dominance in global trade and improved the efficiency of their colonial administration in India.
 
• Since the canal reduced travel time and costs, it enhanced British access to Indian exports like **spices, textiles, and raw materials** and increased their ability to import British goods to India.
 
• The British government purchased a controlling interest in the canal in **1875**, further consolidating their influence over this crucial trade route.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Suez Canal:**

 
 
• The Suez Canal is an **artificial sea-level waterway** in Egypt that connects the **Mediterranean Sea** to the **Red Sea**.
 
• It spans approximately **193 km** and was officially opened in **November 1869**.
 
• The canal provides a direct maritime route between Europe and Asia and is among the most important waterways in global shipping.
 
• The British Empire's acquisition of shares in the Suez Canal in **1875** gave it a strategic advantage in controlling the route to India.
 
 
 
• **Conolly Canal:**
 
 
• The Conolly Canal is located in **Kerala, India**, and was constructed during the British era for irrigation and transportation purposes.
 
• While significant for local trade, it did not have a major impact on British control over India's foreign trade.
 
 
 
• **Buckingham Canal:**
 
 
• The Buckingham Canal is a **man-made waterway** in southern India, primarily used for irrigation and local transportation.
 
• It was constructed during British rule but was not connected to international trade routes like the Suez Canal.
 
 
 
• **Munak Canal:**
 
 
• The Munak Canal is an important irrigation canal in northern India.
 
• Although it facilitates agricultural activities, it is unrelated to India's foreign trade or British control.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Impact of the Suez Canal:**

 
 
• The canal significantly improved trade efficiency between Britain and its colonies, particularly India.
 
• Its strategic importance led to fierce geopolitical competition over its control, culminating in the British acquisition of shares in **1875**.
 
• The Suez Canal remains a critical trade route for global commerce today, handling about **12% of world trade**.
 
 
 
• **British Colonial Trade:**
 
 
• India was a major exporter of **cotton textiles, spices, and indigo** during British rule, and imports included machinery, manufactured goods, and British textiles.
 
• The Suez Canal played a crucial role in facilitating these trade flows.
